name: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
note: Grenada's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: individuals aren't issued a TIN automatically: one is issued only to an individual liable to file a tax return or pay direct tax; it is a six-digit unique number with no other structure. The sheet doesn't name the issuing office; Grenada's Inland Revenue Division is read as the issuer from the sheet's subject (the tax administration), not stated in it. Read as given on application, to anyone liable; `needed` is tax. No check rule, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Grenada: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Individuals [No] Entities [Yes] ... A TIN is only issued to an individual who is liable to file a tax return or pay direct tax ... There is no TIN structure other than the issuing of a six (6) digit unique number
